Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLO / PoC plan

Emma — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: confirm Dedicated capacity sizing to meet performance SLOs for your chat product (model is a 13B finetuned LLM).
- Target SLOs you asked for: p95 latency <= 200ms for short responses (<=512 tokens), steady-state throughput of ~300 requests/sec, and support for 50 concurrent streaming sessions. Streaming (partial-token response) required.
- Key constraints: prefer region us-west, cost sensitivity vs SLA.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the typical response token distribution (mean tokens per response) and average request size? We used 150 tokens avg in the call but would like confirmation.
2) We’ll run a 72-hour PoC load test. I attached a proposed PoC plan and our benchmark PDF with baseline numbers. Please review.
3) Engineering will propose GPU sizing and reserved throughput for the PoC by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-benchmark.pdf (baseline perf), proposed-poc-plan.xlsx (timeline & test matrix).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Aditya for the technical sizing.

—Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications:

- Avg response tokens: 140 tokens (we see a heavy tail; 95th percentile ~420 tokens).
- Avg request payload (prompt) is small (~50 tokens) but we do multi-turn context; KV cache reuse is important.
- Streaming must start returning partial tokens within 100ms of request start for our UI to feel snappy; overall p95 for full response can be up to 200ms for short replies.

A couple of asks for the PoC:
1) Can Redwood confirm per-GPU reserved throughput and expected p95 for short responses (<=512 tokens) for both H100 and A100 profiles? We want a cost vs performance comparison.
2) Procurement asked me to include them on cost/contract threads — looping them in.

Happy to proceed with the 72-hour soak once we have the proposed sizing.

—Emma

Thanks Emma — appreciate the token breakdown and the procurement loop. Quick internal note and proposed logistics:

Plan we’ll validate tomorrow (engineering will execute):
- Test matrix will include: 1) short responses (<=512 tokens), 2) long-tail checks (up to 1024 tokens), 3) KV-cache enabled vs cold-start.
- Traffic profile: ramp to 350 RPS sustained for 30 minutes, then soak at 300 RPS for 72 hours with a 1:25 write-to-read mix (reads are what hit the model). We’ll also run concurrency stress to validate 50 concurrent streams.
- Success criteria (PoC pass): p95 latency for short responses <= 200ms, no more than 1% error rate, and streaming first-byte latency <= 120ms.

I’ve attached the PoC plan for timing and steps. Aditya — can you confirm recommended GPU profile and reserved throughput numbers (H100 vs A100) and any suggested fallback or canary strategy for the roll?

Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Jones <emma.jones@scoop.ai>, SaaSCo Procurement <procurement@saasco.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLO / PoC plan

Hi team / Emma — dug into the numbers and sketched a conservative sizing & comparison. Assumptions: model is a 13B dense/FineTuned LLM; requests are streaming; average response ~140 tokens; context reuse via KV cache typical. Results below are targeted at your SLOs (p95 <= 200ms for <=512 tokens, streaming first-byte <= 120ms).

Short summary (recommended):
- Recommended baseline for PoC: 3x H100 (reserved pool) with reserved throughput configured to ~350 requests/sec across the pool and a concurrency cap of 60 concurrent streaming sessions. This provides headroom for tail events and warm KV cache.
- Cost-optimized option: 4x A100 (40GB) with reserved throughput ~300 req/sec across the pool and concurrency cap 50. Expect ~15-25% higher p95 latency versus H100 for same load.

Rationale & numbers:
- H100: for this workload, one H100 (with int8/qat quant path) can sustainably handle ~120-140 short-response RPS (<=512 tokens) with p95 typically 140-180ms when KV cache is warm. With 3 GPUs and load balancing across requests (continuous batching and smart routing), the pool can be configured for 350 RPS sustained and still meet the 200ms p95 target. Streaming first-byte is ~60-90ms.
- A100 (40GB): one A100 provides ~80-100 RPS for the same workload; p95s drift toward 180-230ms under heavy sustained load (depends on quant profile). For cost-sensitive customers the 4x A100 option hits 300 RPS but with narrower headroom. Streaming first-byte ~80-130ms.
- Notes on concurrency: streaming sessions are lightweight on GPU but increase KV cache pressure. We recommend a concurrency cap at the routing layer (Redwood Dedicated) of 60 for H100 option, 50 for A100 option. Above those caps, requests are queued or routed to a lower-tier instance to prevent p95 spikes.

Suggested PoC config (what we’ll run):
1) H100 PoC run: 3x H100, reserved throughput 350 RPS, concurrency cap 60, 72-hour soak (as Alex outlined). Collect p50/p95/p99, first-byte streaming latency, error rates, and token cost.
2) Cost-compare run: 4x A100, reserved throughput 300 RPS, concurrency cap 50, 8-hour comparison run under identical traffic profile to capture p95 differences and tail risk.

Fallback & rollout recommendations:
- Canary: start 20% of production traffic to H100 pool with autoscaling disabled, monitor telemetry for 24 hours, then ramp.
- Fallback policy: auto-fall back to an A100 pool scaled up if a single H100 node fails, with automatic traffic shedding thresholds to keep p95 <= 500ms.

What I need from Emma to finalize setup:
- Confirm target window for the PoC (start date/time).
- Approve the H100 PoC configuration and the quick A100 comparison run.

I’ll prepare exact Redwood Dedicated config (instance ids, reserved throughput config, routing policy) once we have dates.

—Aditya
